title: Veins of the upper limb (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Upper limb, the shoulder, and the side of the chest wall. It begins at the lower border of teres major, where the basilic vein is joined by the brachial veins, and the cephalic vein joins it near its upper end.
Runs up through the axilla on the medial side of the axillary artery, partly in front of it.
Becomes the subclavian vein at the outer border of the first rib.
Deep parts of the arm. They begin at the elbow, where the veins that accompany the radial and ulnar arteries join.
A pair of veins that run up on either side of the brachial artery, linked by many short cross branches.
Join the basilic vein near the lower border of teres major to form the axillary vein.
Lateral side of the dorsal venous network of the hand, and the skin and superficial tissues of the lateral side of the forearm and arm.

Starts over the anatomical snuffbox and runs up the lateral side of the forearm to the front of the elbow, where the median cubital vein links it to the basilic vein. It continues up the lateral side of biceps brachii and then in the groove between deltoid and pectoralis major, and pierces the clavipectoral fascia just below the clavicle.
Medial side of the dorsal venous network of the hand, and the skin and superficial tissues of the medial side of the forearm and arm.

Runs up the medial side of the forearm and receives the median cubital vein in front of the elbow. A little below the middle of the arm it pierces the deep fascia and then runs up beside the brachial artery.
Joins the brachial veins near the lower border of teres major to form the axillary vein.
Carries blood from the cephalic vein to the basilic vein. It often receives the median antebrachial vein.
Runs upward and medially across the front of the elbow, under the skin of the cubital fossa. The bicipital aponeurosis separates it from the brachial artery and the median nerve.
hy: The vein most often used to draw blood. The bicipital aponeurosis lies between it and the brachial artery and median nerve and gives them some protection.

rows: Superficial veins of the palm and of the front of the forearm.
Runs up the middle of the front of the forearm, between the cephalic and basilic veins. Its size and pattern vary.
Usually the median cubital vein or the basilic vein. Sometimes it splits near the elbow into two veins, one to the cephalic vein and one to the basilic vein.
